title: Pre-meeting brief: Stripe

tldr.text: Stripe has accelerated its AI and crypto strategy, acquiring Bridge for $1.1 billion (Feb 4 2025), Metronome (Jan 14 2026) and agreeing to buy OpenRouter (Aug 19 2026).
Stripe launched Global Payouts, enabling US businesses to send USDC and OUSD to crypto wallets in over 160 markets across nine blockchains.
New products Stripe Pay and multi‑currency stablecoin cards aim to bring instant B2B payments and cross‑border financing to SMBs.

keyDevelopments.text: Stripe launched Global Payouts, allowing US businesses to send USDC and OUSD to crypto wallets in more than 160 markets.
Stripe introduced Stripe Pay, an instant B2B payments solution targeting SMBs.
Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a service that routes AI requests across model providers, on August 19 2026.
Stripe acquired Bridge, a stablecoin issuance and orchestration platform, for $1.1 billion, closing on February 4 2025.

sources.content: The Economics of Stripe's AI Strategy Instinct rolled out a funded shopping agent to eligible US users on October 26. Customers load a Link balance and set a limit for each purchase. Within that limit, the agent can check out without asking again. New York was excluded from the initial rollout. Stripe Crypto described the payment architecture on October 27, a day after Instinct's launch. ( Stripe Crypto@StripeCrypto Stripe Crypto brings together everything needed to enable agentic commerce. From stablecoins on @tempo to secure non-custodial wallets powered by @privy\_io, here's what's powering Link balance for AI agents, starting with @instinct. 4:21 PM · Oct 27, 2026 · 49.7K Views 42 Replies · 50 Reposts · 286 Likes In Instinct's launch flow, Stripe's onramp converts dollars funded by a debit card into stablecoins on Tempo. A Privy noncustodial wallet holds the balance. Link enforces the customer's spending rules, and Stripe Issuing supplies a virtual debit card for checkout. The merchant receives a card payment without integrating crypto. Link's terms specify USDC for the noncustodial agent-wallet balance, despite OUSD being the default elsewhere in Stripe's stablecoin offering. An agent can therefore stay within its budget and still buy the wrong item. Link’s terms generally make the user responsible for those purchasing decisions, while treating payment-execution errors separately and preserving applicable rights. Stripe also offers protections for qualifying agent purchases, initially through Muse. Their availability depends on the agent and transaction; the announcement did not establish coverage for Instinct orders. For Stripe, the commercial question is how much of the activity before checkout it can turn into a paid service: model selection, billing, spending authorization and the movement of funds. sources.title: Stripe offers US stablecoin payouts to wallets in 160+ markets
sources.snippet:
The October announcement placed Global Payouts alongside Treasury and Issuing in a shared financial services offering. Stripe said the products can share customer verification information and work with Open Standard’s OUSD stablecoin and the Tempo blockchain.

## USDC payouts support nine blockchain networks

The supported USDC networks are Arbitrum, Avalanche C-Chain, Base, Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, Solana, Stellar and Tempo. OUSD payouts are available on Base, Ethereum, Solana and Tempo.

Before sending funds, Stripe instructs businesses to check that the recipient’s wallet supports both the selected stablecoin and the chosen network. [...] At the time, Stripe said businesses could send instant stablecoin payouts to recipients in 160 markets and traditional currency payouts to more than 100 markets directly through its Dashboard.

The announcement described hosted forms and APIs for fintech companies that want to build payouts into their own products. Named uses included loan disbursements, remittances, investment withdrawals and neobank cash-outs.

The rise of embedded finance has led businesses to expect payments to fit seamlessly into the platforms and workflows they already use. Yet business-to-business payments often remain time-consuming and costly. Stripe is looking to simplify the process with a service that resembles the consumer peer-to-peer payment experience. Businesses could search for a vendor’s profile and transfer funds via the Stripe Pay plug-in. For companies that lack a recipient’s full payment details, Stripe also offers a business directory. “Stripe is trying to make paying another business as easy as sending money to a handle,” said Brian Riley, Director of Credit at Javelin Strategy & Research. “Businesses can identify recipients through their Stripe profiles instead of entering traditional bank details. The real headline may be ‘free’ not ‘instant,’ as Stripe Pay is advertising these business-to-business transfers with no transfer fee.” Providing Clarity and Control Several trends are driving demand for better B2B payment solutions. The growth of vertical software-as-a-service platforms has given businesses of all sizes access to industry-specific tools, with seamless payment acceptance central to the model. Meanwhile, the consumer payments experience has raised expectations for B2B transactions to be digital-first and easy to use. Beyond convenience, payment efficiency has implications for cash flow and working capital. This is one reason virtual cards have gained traction. They give organizations greater control over payment timing and more visibility into spending and liquidity. Whether Stripe Pay can deliver similar advantages will depend on how businesses use the service and how it integrates with their existing payment processes. Stripe acquired Bridge, a stablecoin orchestration platform, for $1.1 billion. The acquisition closed in February 2025, and one source specifies February 4, 2025.

### Has Stripe bought Privy?

Reports describe a Stripe acquisition of Privy, a crypto-wallet company. The purchase price and completion date remain unconfirmed in the sources we reviewed, so we do not state either.

### Is the OpenRouter deal done?

Reports describe an agreement, not a completed acquisition. The estimated value of $7 billion to $8 billion is unconfirmed. Watch for an official announcement before treating the number as settled.
